assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its conversion into durable therapies has transformed type 2 diabetes care and obesity treatment, with broad cardiometabolic benefit. It combines fundamental hormone physiology with exceptional clinical and societal impact; the central nervous system appetite effects also appeal from a neuroendocrine perspective.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and characterization of the active peptide in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, therapeutic rationale) and Mojsov (peptide identification and early synthesis/activity) are the strongest three from the supplied names. Knudsen's drug-development role is real but industrial; Habener-type early contributors are not on the supplied list, so credit allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized outcome trials, widespread clinical adoption and years of independent confirmation. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first identified the active GLP-1(7-36) form; the credited list omits some early contributors; I cannot independently verify every historical claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, converting chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition. The concept is clear, original and has had lasting influence across oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery/chemistry-biology program), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Contributions by Janet Rowley, Nowell/Hungerford, and the BCR-ABL gene discovery are earlier foundational work not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of survival data and independent replication. Recognition is timely; the Lasker award has already acknowledged it.
uncertainties: Whether the earlier Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL fusion discoveries would need recognition alongside the drug work; the credited list is restricted to the drug-development contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are a rare case of a prize-level discovery with demonstrated cancer prevention at population level, including near-elimination of cervical lesions in vaccinated cohorts. The VLP concept is original and the impact on public health is large.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer contributed to the early VLP work and the Australian co-development. Zhou and others also contributed to early VLP expression and there is a known priority complexity, which is an attribution risk. A zur Hausen already received the 2008 prize for HPV-cancer link.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long-term population effectiveness data from several countries; independent confirmation is strong. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority and patent dispute around early VLP work (Frazer and Zhou); relation to the earlier 2008 prize may be judged as partly covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with approved products and an expanding field including autoimmunity applications. Importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulated CAR design), June (clinical translation in CLL, 4-1BB CAR) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early clinical proof) offer a plausible trio; Eshhar, Gross and others are not on the supplied list, and the chimeric receptor concept has contested origins.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature in hematologic malignancy with several years of follow-up, but toxicity, solid-tumor limitations and manufacturing issues remain, so the final scope is not settled.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept; incomplete evidence for solid tumors; long-term safety including secondary malignancies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provides cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has revolutionized experimental neuroscience, enabling causal circuit studies and early translational efforts such as vision restoration. Originality and methodological impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin function, Deisseroth led the neuronal application and widespread dissemination. Boyden, Miesenböck, Bamberg and others are also strong, so a three-person limit forces a contested choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with massive independent adoption; clinical translation is still early, so the physiological or medical benefit is more indirect.
uncertainties: Six-person credit pool exceeds the three-laureate limit; competing claims by Boyden, Miesenböck and Bamberg; clinical impact still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation gave an effective and reversible treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease and opened neuromodulation for tremor, dystonia and other disorders. It has changed clinical practice for many thousands of patients and illuminated basal ganglia circuit function.
assessment.attribution: Benabid introduced high-frequency thalamic and subthalamic stimulation; the supplied credit lists only him. Contributions of DeLong and Bergman (circuit rationale) and others such as Limousin are not in the supplied credit and could matter for a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of clinical use and randomized trials confirm benefit. Recognition is timely, with a Lasker award already given.
uncertainties: Single-name credit may not capture circuit-model contributions and the shared clinical development; I cannot verify detailed priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) transformed spinal muscular atrophy from a lethal childhood disease to a treatable one and established splice-modulating antisense therapy for CNS disease. The mechanistic insight and clinical effect are striking.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a natural pairing; Adrian Krainer's collaborators and Ionis colleagues might also warrant discussion, and the discovery of SMN1 by Melki is not included.
assessment.maturity: Increasingly mature, with several years of long-term follow-up, though it is a relatively recent therapy; recognition is plausible but could still await longer evidence.
uncertainties: Relation to the SMN1 gene discovery and to other SMA therapies; long-term durability; possible preference to recognize antisense or RNA therapeutics more broadly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a key driver of rheumatoid inflammation and that its blockade is effective launched biologic therapy for autoimmune disease, with major benefit across arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease. Importance, clarity and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly developed the concept and clinical proof; the credit is tidy for two laureates. Other contributions (anti-TNF antibody engineering, Vilcek, Cerami) could complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of clinical use and confirmation; recognition has already been extensive (Lasker award), so timeliness is not a concern.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with credit for antibody engineering and TNF biology; the field's best-known figures may not align neatly with a two-person configuration.
